newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh brokers rigged market - report.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh brokers rigged market - report.

text.p: Leading brokers on Bangladesh's two bourses have been implicated by a government-commissioned report for their alleged involvement in price manipulation, newspapers said on Friday.
"The enquiry committee on the share scam has identified at least 20 dealers of the Dhaka and Chittagong bourses as responsible for the recent manipulation of share prices," The Daily Star said.

The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) chairman said on Friday that he had reports from the committee. "Action will be taken against those responsible as per the existing law of the country," Harunur Rashid told Reuters.
Most Bangladeshi dailies published reports on the probe into developments in the stock market during July-November last year. The report is expected to be made public later.

The newspapers said top dealers, including some senior members of the Dhaka Stock Exchange (DSE), were involved in the scam. The Star quoted the report as saying the identified brokers were involved in insider trading.
The committee, headed by Aminul Islam, professor of economics at Jahangirnagar University, submitted the 84-page report to the SEC chairman on Thursday.
SEC sources said offenders in the scandal could be fined, jailed or face expulsion from the DSE under the existing law.
The newspapers said the report also identified some companies that manipulated share prices in the kerb market through their agents.
The market began climbing after elections last June that brought Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina to power. By October the DSE benchmark index had jumped from less than 1,000 to more than 3,600.

A peaceful political atmosphere and government measures, including the offer of bank loans to investors and removal of a three-year lock-in period for foreign investors on trading of initial public offerings (IPOs), lured thousands of people to trade securities in the unofficial kerb market.
In November, the SEC imposed circuit breakers, or caps, on price movement to stabilise the market and warned against trading in 24 companies with poor financial track records.
The share prices have been falling since the SEC squeezed the daily price movement limit to five percent in November from 10 percent to calm the overheated market.

The Financial Express said influential brokers including a foreign brokerage firm were involved in irregularities. "Some important DSE functionaries and also a head of a foreign investment company were allegedly involved in irregularities on DVP (delivery versus payment) dealings," it said.

"The DVP dealings were mostly done between authorised brokers and were not actually made effective, only to allow the share prices to move up and up in order to reap windfall gains," said a market analyst. "You can call it false trading."
More than 100 out of nearly 190 listed brokers on Thursday met to review the market situation and demanded the resignation of DSE council members.
The DSE has an elected nine-member council, headed by the DSE chairman, to monitor trading activities in the bourse.
Police on Thursday drove away hundreds of kerb market traders, who were protesting falling prices and demanding that those responsible for manipulating share prices be punished.
The DSE index gained 82.63 points or 7.68 percent to 1,157.58 at the close of Thursday's trading. Friday is the weekend in Moslem Bangladesh.
